finding: Soccer Half Time markets generate purely phantom edge. 25 resolved Half Time signals since 2026-07-03 (all soccer, all backs, avg edge claimed ~8pp) show a 24.0% win rate at average odds 4.21 — break-even at those odds is 23.7%, so the real edge is ~0. The smoking gun is that 8 of 16 unique HT events (50%) fired 2-3 mutually-exclusive signals in the same 3-way market (Brazil AND Norway; France AND Morocco; Hammarby AND Kalmar AND Draw; Craiova AND Cluj AND Draw — for a single match only one outcome can win, so the model cannot possibly have positive edge on both/all sides simultaneously). Net paper P&L: -£19.06.
root_cause: Half Time is a 3-outcome market (Home/Draw/Away for the first half only). The keyword model was trained/designed for single-winner and 2-way markets: it scores each contract in isolation against the Wang-transformed market probability, so a market whose implied probs sum to ~105% before Wang and ~90% after Wang can appear to give +7-9pp edge on ALL three outcomes. There is no cross-outcome sanity check. First-half goals are also much rarer than full-match goals, so the model's full-match keyword vocabulary (form/injury/strong) has no predictive relevance to half-time state. BUG-130 originally blocked this exact market type as phantom-edge junk in 2026-06; MOD-198 re-whitelisted it in a blanket 'unblock everything the scanner fetches' sweep with no performance evidence; the current data confirms the original block was correct. Precedent: MOD-305 removed 'completed match' from the same whitelist in 2026-07-03 for structurally identical reasons (unwinnable-by-keyword-model market producing phantom signals).
proposed_change: In scripts/analyze_research.py, remove the entry `"half time",` on line 96 from the SUPPORTED_MARKET_PATTERNS list (leave the comment context intact — the block above that list is the shared documentation for the whole whitelist). This one edit blocks the market at two points because researcher.py imports SUPPORTED_MARKET_PATTERNS as a single source of truth: (a) no more research budget spent on Half Time markets at selection time in researcher.py, (b) no more signals emitted from Half Time markets in analyze_research.py's signal loop. Also removes 'Half Time/Full Time' as a side-effect since it contains the substring 'half time' (n=4 in the same window, 25.0% WR, -£4.02 — same pathology, same fix). No config change required. Log a MOD entry (e.g. MOD-336) and add a BUGS.md pointer mirroring the MOD-305 comment pattern already at line 87-95.
expected_impact: Eliminates ~25-30 phantom Half Time signals per 21-day window (derived from actual: 25 in 21 days). Direct paper-P&L saving of ~£20/window on removed losing signals, and reclaims ~30 research slots for markets with a real edge signal. Overall win-rate arithmetic: removing 6 wins from 25 phantom trades moves the resolved-window WR from 40.0% (175/437) to 41.0% (169/412). Brier score should also improve marginally: HT signals are structurally miscalibrated (model_prob ~30-40% on outcomes whose true prob equals market_prob ~24-30%), so removing them removes a chunk of consistent miscalibration. These numbers are derived directly from the resolved-trade data, not guessed.
test_condition: After the change, run one full routine (any of the 7 daily cron slots) and confirm zero new signals in data/paper_tracker.json where market_name contains 'Half Time' (case-insensitive). Then over the next 14 days verify: (a) count of new HT trades logged = 0, (b) resolved-trade WR on non-HT markets is unchanged (should remain ~41-42% for backs — no collateral damage), (c) research-slot utilization report from researcher.py shows the reclaimed HT slots being spent on other markets in the same category. Sample size for verdict: 100+ new resolved trades across other market types (~2 weeks at current volume) to be confident nothing else regressed. Reversion is trivial: re-add the `"half time",` line.

Same probe-only caveat; also consistent with MOD-293's 'high-edge backs on 3-way markets = phantom' hypothesis — could sharpen max_credible_edge_pct or add a market-arity check for backs on 3-way markets, but overlaps materially with this Half Time finding (same root cause: keyword model on 3-way markets).

New-sport LAY probes (darts, snooker, boxing, australian_rules) aggregated: n=19, 5.3% WR (1 win), -£11.22 since the 2026-07-23 rollout. Very early — MOD-316 stipulates n>=30 per (sport, market-type) segment before promotion/kill, and no individual sport has reached that threshold (darts n=7, boxing n=5, aus_rules n=4, snooker n=3). Worth flagging next cycle if the trend continues; too early to act.
Match Odds 7-9pp LAYs are 5.9% WR (n=17) — devastating but small sample and spread across sports; hard to derive a clean rule from it yet.
caveats: n=25 is a modest sample for HT specifically, but the phantom-edge mechanism is deterministic (verifiable a priori: 8 of 16 events with multi-side signals is impossible under a genuinely calibrated model), not merely a statistical underperformance. The finding also has strong prior support (BUG-130's original block, MOD-305's identical precedent) so the evidentiary bar is lower than for a novel claim. HT signals are all backs and all probe-tracked (signal_track='standard' but MOD-280 suppresses back placement), so the £19 loss is paper-only — the direct dollar impact of the fix is small in the short term; the larger value is (a) reclaiming research budget for markets with real edge, and (b) preventing this segment from being 'promoted' later on the strength of an artifact. Category tag on HT signals is uniformly 'soccer' — no cross-sport contamination like the earlier soccer:multi:match_odds finding (see [[project_session_jul13]]).
